title: Tallest waterfalls
measure: Total height in metres, from the top of the waterfall to the bottom, including all its drops. Most of these fall in several tiers, so the longest single drop is often much less. Figures follow the World Waterfall Database, the main reference for waterfall heights.

entries.name: Angel Falls
entries.note: Also the tallest uninterrupted drop on Earth: 807 m in a single plunge from the Auyán-tepui plateau.
entries.source: World Waterfall Database, via WorldAtlas and Victoria Falls Guide

entries.name: Tugela Falls
entries.note: Falls in five tiers, the longest 411 m. A 2016 survey claimed 983 m, which would make it taller than Angel Falls; that figure isn't widely accepted yet.
entries.source: World Waterfall Database, via WorldAtlas and Victoria Falls Guide

entries.name: Tres Hermanas
entries.note: "Three Sisters": named for its three drops.
entries.source: World Waterfall Database, via WorldAtlas and Victoria Falls Guide

entries.name: Olo'upena Falls
entries.note: Pours straight down sea cliffs and can only be seen from the air or the sea.
entries.source: World Waterfall Database, via WorldAtlas and Victoria Falls Guide

entries.name: Yumbilla
